_comment: Options for the ndX 'FRET calibration' action. The factor toggles are the point: the calibration always runs in full, but only the selected factors are written into the window, so a gamma determined on a reference sample is not replaced by a worse one fitted from this measurement's own populations. The background is a separate choice because it is an input rather than something the calibration determines. The Populations panel chooses population-wise gamma (tttrlib's species_factors, as off / auto / on) and the gating dimensions; the app disables the dimensions the loaded table has no column for.

sections.title: Determine
sections.description: Which correction factors this calibration is allowed to change. The others keep the value the window already has.

sections.label: α leakage
sections.description: Donor emission detected in the acceptor channel. Taken from the donor-only population, so it needs one.

sections.label: δ direct excitation
sections.description: Acceptor excited by the donor laser. Taken from the acceptor-only population, so it needs one.

sections.label: γ detection / QY
sections.description: Detection efficiency times quantum-yield ratio. From the 1/S = Ω + Σ·E fit across FRET sub-populations, or from the donor lifetime. Turn this off to keep a γ you determined on a reference sample.

sections.label: β excitation flux
sections.description: Ratio of the two lasers' excitation flux and cross-sections. Comes from the same E-S fit as γ.

sections.label: R₀ Förster radius
sections.description: Not a correction factor — it converts efficiency to distance. Off by default: it belongs to the dye pair and its environment, not to this measurement.

sections.title: Background
sections.description: Backgrounds are an input to the calibration, not one of its factors — unless you ask it to fit them, which is what 'fit' does.

sections.label: Take from
sections.description:
'fit' determines them from the reference populations themselves — an acceptor-only burst has no donor, so what appears in the donor channel is background; a donor-only burst has no acceptor, so what appears under acceptor excitation is background; and the leakage line I_DA = α·I_DD + bg_da gives the third as its intercept. Use this when the background is not known, which is most of the time. It costs a second calibration pass: the populations have to exist before they can be read, and once the background is subtracted the classification is made again.

'measurement' uses the rates the Background step stored in this measurement's container, multiplied by each burst's duration — so a 4 ms burst carries four times the background of a 1 ms one, which a single number cannot express. Falls back to the window's constants if the container has no stored estimate.

'constants' uses the window's Bg / Br / By as they stand. 'none' sets them to zero.

This is the correction whose error is hardest to see: it moves the dim bursts and leaves the bright ones, which looks exactly like a real sub-population.

sections.label: Min. reference bursts
sections.description: Smallest donor-only / acceptor-only population accepted when fitting a background. Below it that channel is left at whatever it had rather than guessed from a handful of bursts.

sections.title: Populations
sections.description: Whether the correction factors may differ between the FRET populations, and what the populations are told apart by. A population-wise γ is written as a vector constant (γ[FRET 1], γ[FRET 2]…) that the Parameters tab lists as an expandable row; to go back to one value, right-click it there and choose Make scalar.

sections.label: Population-wise factors
sections.description:
One γ for all FRET populations, or one per population. A local environment can change a dye's quantum yield in one population, and with it that population's γ; β, α and δ stay shared.

'Off' writes one global factor set, as before — the per-population model is not tried.
'Auto' (default) fits both a shared and a per-population γ and keeps the per-population one only when it lowers the BIC.
'On' writes the per-population γ whenever it is identifiable, even when the BIC prefers the shared one.

Per-population γ is only identifiable with lifetimes: every FRET population needs a donor lifetime (the static FRET line pins its E), and there must be at least two populations. Without a donor lifetime column all three modes give the same scalar result. Written γ vectors appear in the Parameters tab; right-click > Make scalar removes one again. The test itself is cheap; it is the gating dimensions below that cost time.

sections.label: Population finder
sections.description: How the donor-only, acceptor-only and FRET populations are found in the gating dimensions. 'HDBSCAN' (default) finds dense clusters of any shape and leaves sparse bursts unassigned, so a smeared or non-Gaussian population is not split into several components or merged with a neighbour; outliers are removed per dimension before the dimensions are scaled. 'Gaussian mixture' fits Gaussian components and picks their number by the BIC. On cal1 with S+E the mixture took 45 s and lost the donor-only class; HDBSCAN took 3 s. Only used when gating dimensions beyond S are chosen. Needs a tttrlib whose calibration has the population_method option; otherwise this choice is disabled and the Gaussian mixture is used.

sections.title: Gating dimensions
sections.description: What the populations are told apart by. S alone is the stoichiometry gating (fast, the default); any other ticked dimension switches to the multidimensional mixture over all ticked ones, about ten times slower (25 s instead of 2.4 s on cal1). Dimensions this measurement has no column for are disabled; their tooltip says which column is missing.

sections.label: S stoichiometry
sections.description: Corrected stoichiometry, computed from the counts, so every ALEX/PIE measurement has it. Ticked alone it is the stoichiometry gating the calibration always used (fast).

sections.label: E efficiency
sections.description: Corrected FRET efficiency, computed from the counts. Ticking it switches to the multidimensional mixture over every ticked dimension, which separates FRET populations the stoichiometry alone lumps together. Cost: the multidimensional gating is about ten times slower than the stoichiometry gating (25 s instead of 2.4 s on the cal1 measurement, 44 270 bursts).

sections.label: τ_D donor lifetime
sections.description: Per-burst donor lifetime. Separates species at equal E but different lifetime (dynamics, a changed quantum yield), and it is what makes population-wise γ identifiable. Cost: the multidimensional gating is about ten times slower than the stoichiometry gating (25 s instead of 2.4 s on the cal1 measurement, 44 270 bursts).

sections.label: τ_A acceptor lifetime
sections.description: Per-burst acceptor lifetime. Tracks the acceptor quantum yield of each population, the usual reason a population has its own γ. Cost: the multidimensional gating is about ten times slower than the stoichiometry gating (25 s instead of 2.4 s on the cal1 measurement, 44 270 bursts).

sections.label: r_D donor anisotropy
sections.description: Per-burst donor anisotropy: separates populations whose donor is stuck. Cost: the multidimensional gating is about ten times slower than the stoichiometry gating (25 s instead of 2.4 s on the cal1 measurement, 44 270 bursts).

sections.label: r_A acceptor anisotropy
sections.description: Per-burst acceptor anisotropy: separates populations whose acceptor is stuck. Cost: the multidimensional gating is about ten times slower than the stoichiometry gating (25 s instead of 2.4 s on the cal1 measurement, 44 270 bursts).

sections.label: γ from
sections.description: 'es' is the 1/S = Ω + Σ·E fit and needs at least two FRET sub-populations; 'lifetime' uses the static FRET line and works on a single population, but needs a per-burst donor lifetime and a trustworthy τ_D(0); 'combined' is the precision-weighted mean; 'auto' takes the E-S fit and falls back to the lifetime. The two routes are independent, so their disagreement is itself a diagnostic.

sections.label: Use light-path priors
sections.description: Combine the data estimates with the optical model's excitation/emission probabilities, so the result is a posterior: data where the data speaks, optics where it does not.

sections.label: Bootstrap resamples
sections.description: Resamples used for the factor uncertainties, with the population assignment held fixed. 0 skips them. It is cheap — the classification, not the resampling, is what costs.

sections.label: τ_D(0) (ns)
sections.description: Donor-only lifetime, which anchors the static FRET line. Only used by the lifetime route; a wrong value there shows up as γ disagreeing between the two routes.

sections.label: Linker σ (Å)
sections.description: Width of the dye-linker distance distribution, which sets the curvature of the static FRET line.

sections.label: Add accurate E / S / R_DA columns
sections.description: Write the corrected per-burst columns under new names. Not redundant with applying the constants: ndX's own efficiency equation has no direct-excitation term, so constants alone cannot make its native column accurate. Its own columns are left untouched.

sections.title: When it finishes
sections.description: Where the result is kept. The measurement container is the default: it already holds the photons, the burst table and the background estimate, and a calibration determined from them belongs in the same file.

sections.label: Store the calibration in the measurement
sections.description: Writes the factors, their uncertainties and the report into the .pto container the bursts came from. Each save is kept as its own object, so an earlier calibration is still there afterwards. With no container, the report window offers a file instead.
